title: Value of a Bearer Authorization header for a Figma token
summary: A synthetic opaque value after the Bearer scheme in an Authorization header, in a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map; the value has no documented prefix or width.
rationale: Figma documents the OAuth access token as passed in a Bearer authorization header and the SCIM API token as included in an Authorization header using Bearer, so one header carries both families and the header does not say which. This is a different carrier from the X-Figma-Token header of the personal access token. The value is flagged because of where it sits, not because of any prefix, length or alphabet, none of which the cited pages state. The extent is the header value only.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value after the Bearer scheme in an Authorization header is treated as a credential whatever its shape and covered whole. Figma documents the OAuth access token and the SCIM API token as sent in an Authorization header using Bearer (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic authorization attribution are the project's decisions. No prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: The API token must be included in an Authorization header using Bearer when calling any of the SCIM methods.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
